html:
The ongoing US-Iran war and escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz dominate global headlines today, with both Washington and Tehran navigating complex diplomatic and military maneuvers while major powers like Russia engage in peacemaking efforts. Trump has stated that no new attack on Iran will occur before the US midterm elections in November, despite US sanctions targeting 17 vessels of Iran’s "shadow fleet." Meanwhile, Iran’s nuclear chief affirms that Iran will not abandon uranium enrichment or hand over its uranium. Iran also reports "explosions" in Hormuz, with an IRGC advisor stating the Strait is closed until Iran's demands are met, a claim rejected by US CentCom.

Russia-Ukraine War: The protracted conflict in Ukraine continues with Russian strikes on public buses in Kyiv leaving 30 dead and worsening blackouts, while Moscow is reportedly closing in on Ukraine's "fortress belt." The long-range aerial war persists amid a ground deadlock, and military representatives from all 32 NATO member states have met in Kyiv. Separately, Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are slated to meet Ukrainian negotiators and European officials in Miami to discuss new peace proposals. In the Black Sea, drone attacks, suspected to be Russian, have sunk three Turkish-owned cargo ships in EU waters, with ten Egyptian and Syrian crew missing, heightening concerns over regional security.

Middle East Security: The conflict in Yemen has seen Iran-aligned Houthis claim a ballistic missile attack on Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh airport, damaging a plane and leading some airlines to suspend flights. Saudi officials confirm three deaths and dozens of injuries at civilian airports earlier this week, with a nursery reportedly hit by debris. Regional and international bodies, including the Palestinian Presidency, have condemned these Houthi attacks. Simultaneously, an Israeli soldier was killed and three were wounded in south Lebanon, adding to ongoing tensions in the Levant, while Israeli forces killed seven in Gaza, including a Palestinian child.

Korean Peninsula Tensions: South Korea has test-flown its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon, following a similar test by North Korea, intensifying regional anxieties. South Korea also announced it would recall its ambassador to Ukraine after Ukraine reportedly refused to apologize for the public revelation of a North Korean prisoner of war transfer, a move President Lee Jae Myung had threatened with unspecified punitive steps.

Global Economy & Social Unrest: The Australian market saw a significant event as Firmus pulled what was set to be the biggest ASX float since 1997, amid investor doubt over its AI datacentre business. In Europe, Spain faces a growing housing crisis, with protests blaming "vulture funds" and the Spanish prime minister calling a snap election following the death of Maricarmen Abascal, whose eviction sparked widespread anger. France also continues to experience nationwide student protests, with barricades and police intervention reported in Parisian high schools.

US Domestic Developments: The Pentagon announced that the execution by firing squad of Fort Hood attacker Nidal Malik Hasan will be livestreamed, a decision Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth called "public," though a legal expert termed it "unprecedented" and on "uncertain legal terrain." This comes as a judge ordered evidence preserved from the botched execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee. Separately, an ICE agent shot and injured a man in New York City during an enforcement operation, sparking local protests.
